reviews.name: Sourav Dutta
reviews.text:
We stayed at Padma Homestay in Dhore for 2 days and it was a wonderful experience!
The homestay is very clean, peaceful and feels like home. The room was well-maintained with comfortable bedding and hot water available despite the cold. The views from the homestay are amazing - perfect for relaxing.
The best part is the hospitality. The family is extremely warm, welcoming and helpful. They treated us like family and helped with everything we needed. The home-cooked food was fresh, tasty and served with love.
If you are looking for a calm, budget-friendly and homely stay in Dhore, Padma Homestay is the best choice. Highly recommended. We will definitely come back again!
Thank you for making our stay so memorable.

reviews.name: Jeet
reviews.text:
We stayed at Padma Homestay at Dhotrey while planning our Tonglu trek. Initially we had booked the place for just one night, but by the time we were supposed to leave, none of us really wanted to go.
We reached around 5 PM in the rain, completely unprepared for the cold especially me, standing there in a T-shirt and shorts and literally shivering! But the moment we stepped inside, their warmth and hospitality made us forget the weather outside. They served us steaming hot rice with delicious Bengali homemade dishes, and after a long journey, that meal felt like absolute heaven.
The rooms were cosy, the atmosphere was peaceful, and the hospitality was genuinely heartfelt. But what made our stay truly special was Padma Didi and her family. She has the sweetest little six year young daughter, Rinchen and as luck would have it, her birthday was on September 5th. So, instead of leaving, we extended our stay and got to be part of their little home celebration.
And honestly it didn't feel like we were guests at a homestay anymore it felt like we were celebrating in our own home. We danced, sang, ate wonderful homemade food, laughed endlessly and had an absolute banger of a night.
A very special mention to our group's little bundle of energy Chini, who made sure absolutely nobody was sitting quietly and had everyone dancing their hearts out!
There are certain trips you remember for the places you visit, and then there are trips you remember for the people you meet. Our two days at Padma Homestay belong firmly to the second category. For those two days, we never once felt away from home. Padma Didi and her family welcomed us with so much warmth, affection and generosity that leaving actually felt a little difficult.
Highly recommended for anyone looking for a cosy, authentic and genuinely homely stay at Dhotrey.

reviews.name: Mmanish Hazrra
reviews.text: I stayed for two days at Padma Homestay, Dhotrey. The owner and other stakeholders treated us as a family members. Rooms were very clean, the provided us all kind of possible amenities for our comfort. Talking about foods, I experienced the quality. Since morning to night they delivered warm, fresh and tasty foods. We got the best view of Kunchanjungafromr our room. We were fully satisfied.

reviews.name: Doli Mallick
reviews.text:
Recently, we stayed for two days at Padma Homestay. We were in Room No. 10 (view room) of the new building. The room was quite nice and clean, and the bathroom was also clean. Hot water was available all the time. The dining area is downstairs, and the food was quite good and tasty.
The homestay is run by Padma Di, her brother-in-law, and his wife. All of them are very cooperative and helpful. Since it’s very cold there, they always provided both hot and cold drinking water whenever needed.
We were lucky to see Kanchenjunga on both days. It is visible from our room, and the view is even better from the rooftop.
Dhotrey itself is a very beautiful place. We explored the surrounding areas on foot. A short walk away, there is a Shiva temple, a monastery, and a viewpoint. Another road leads towards Sandakphu.
In the evening, Padma herself does karaoke 🤓. It’s quite enjoyable to listen to—gives a bit of a Goa vibe in the mountains! However, some people might feel it disturbs their sleep at night.
We would love to visit Dhotrey again, and we might stay at Padma Homestay again as well

reviews.name: niladdit saha
reviews.text:
Padma Homestay probably is the best place to stay at Dhotrey.
I've seen negative reviews about this place and have wondered how low the concept of trekking has gone down to. This is a homestay, which is supposed to give you a chance to live WITH them, they are not supposed to host you like a hotel.
Nice, modest, clean rooms with adequate blankets provided. Fully functional toilets with faucets and flush operational, unless temperature dips below freezing point.
Geysers available. All around balcony provides marvellous views. Top floor rooms have a dedicated dining space.
Common dining space is at the lowest floor with heating arrangement. Seating arrangements on floor. Delicious meals (full course meals, that are usually rare on trek routes) with amazing hospitality. Hot water and black tea is available all the time, just ask them.
Tip: Homestays are best enjoyed if you talk to people. Talk to the owners, talk to other guests, share stories and food supplies, stay at the dining space most of the time. Don't expect hotel amenities and don't expect Kanchenjunga all the time, you get those if you're fortunate!

Coming to service and hospitality, it's just spellbound. They take care of their every guest like a family.
The best part is the mouthwatering food.. they serve food in "Kasar thala". Mainly the chicken kosha that they serve in dinner is out of the world.

reviews.name: Kōhī San
reviews.text:
Had issue with water, every time we sat for lunch or dinner, they didn't even bother to give us drinking water in that freezing temperature while they were serving water to others. Not sure why this discrimination. Had to ask for water every single time.
We had to ask about meal timing as it was not written anywhere like other places we visited. We were told snacks would be given in the room at 5pm. Unfortunately waited till 6:30pm but the food was still not ready, kept waiting for more than an hour. They should have atleast told us that they might be late so that we could plan our day accordingly. No proper communication, everybody seemed busy and in rush.
Had no water in room/washroom since evening, had to wait till almost midnight for water after asking for several times and ultimately had to call Padma at 11pm frustratingly for it as we were hell tired after our Trek that day since morning.
Rooms filled with mold, cold air rushing in room from the wide space below the door. Bathroom height too short for tall people.
While booking, the pic showed 2 lampshades in the room, found only 1 when entered the room. Also the room was so poorly lit that couldn't see anything properly even after switching on all the lights after sunset.
Not a good experience we had there. Wouldn't recommend. You can find other better homestay in that location for sure.

Padma didi manages the kitchen almost on her own. So there might not be too many variations in the menu. And that's absolutely fine with me. Some rooms have views, some have not. Rooms are not also equal in size. But the rooms are very clean and well maintained.

reviews.name: Sourav Bose
reviews.text:
Dhotrey, a small village of hope. We know dhotrey for Padma Di who runs a homestay in Dhotrey and mostly the first homestay in Dhotrey . She has a huge contribution in making dhotrey a tourism site. I must say this is the best homestay if you want to stay in a homely atmosphere. Charges are very low there and the behaviour, most importantly food ,all are priceless. Dhotrey is in the buffer area of singalila national forest so dont hope for a good network, but you will get wifi at homestay. U will get 24x7 hot water and if there is an issue with the geyser, padma di takes care of that. Please visit Dhotrey with a mind set that this is not an urban area. YOU ARE GOING TO A FOREST AREA. If you want to make your Dhotrey trip memorable, stay at PADMA HOMESTAY . Otherwise there are plenty of stays which are not homestays rather hotels which are just named as homestays and obviously not homely . Padma homestay is our hideout place and will be for forever .
1. Rooms are nice with pahaar vibes
2. The food is tasty as hell ( chicken kosha and tibetan bun recommended with dolle mirch pickle) . Padma di always provides an excess quantity of food so that no one stays hungry at any cost. Breakfast, lunch, snacks , dinner all included with the package .
3. Once you stay there, you will never feel like you are out of your home.
4. Behaviour is awesome
Thank you Padma di and all the people there at Padma Homestay for making each and every visit super special.

reviews.text:
PADMA HOMESTAY - DHOTREY, DARJEELING ❤️😊
We often say that Sometimes words can't express the feeling of the moments, this goes to same here. Dhotrey is a beautiful village nestled in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, India. Here, We spent 1 day, and this short time is mesmerizing all I can say. This Located at an elevation of approximately 8,500 feet within the buffer zone of Singalila National Park, it's an ideal destination for nature lovers seeking a peaceful escape.
